questions.question: A bad commit reached main, a shared branch. What is the safe way to undo it?
options: git revert: a new commit that undoes it
questions.explanation: Revert keeps history, so it is safe on shared branches.

questions.question: What does git rebase do?
options: Replays your commits on top of another branch, rewriting them

questions.question: A pull request is a feature of…
options: The hosting platform, not of Git

questions.question: Which branching model does the delivery research recommend?
options: Trunk-based: short branches merged to main many times a day
Git flow with long-lived develop and release branches

questions.question: Continuous delivery vs continuous deployment: what is the difference?
options: Delivery keeps one manual approval before release; deployment has none
Deployment needs a manual approval; delivery does not
They are two names for the same thing
Delivery is for libraries, deployment is for services

questions.question: "Build once, deploy many" means…
options: The same artifact goes through every environment; only configuration changes
Each environment builds its own image
Each developer builds locally and pushes

questions.question: Why tag a container image with the commit hash?
options: Every running version points back to its exact code

questions.question: Which strategy sends a small share of traffic to the new version, then grows it?
How do you rename a database column without downtime?
options: Expand and contract: backward-compatible steps, so old and new code both work
Rename it during a maintenance window
Roll back the code if it fails
Use a feature flag on the column
questions.explanation: Code can go back in seconds. Data cannot.
